commit_message:
[Codegen] Compare binding ordinals only within one pipeline layout

A binding ordinal is an index into the binding list of a specific pipeline
layout, so ordinals from two different layouts describe unrelated positions.
mayAlias compared them anyway and reported binding(0) of one layout and
binding(1) of another as disjoint.

Two subspans reach the ordinal comparison whenever both operands resolve to a
binding, so the case never fell through to the AliasAnalysis fallback. Treat
differing layouts as may-alias and record the case in the table.

commit_message:
[Codegen] Support multi-output consumers with permuted indexing maps

Extend lowering of fused & tiled consumer ops from the basic case
(strictly identical indexing over the output operands). We now generalize
the logic for input indexing to support different output maps that are
simple permutations.

This allows to support some fusion cases where a simple transposition
from one of the consumer's connections get fused into the elementwise
generic, and then the consumer gets fused & tiled together with the
matmul. Whether we want such consumer fusion is a separate matter
subject to performance investigations, and in my reproducer there'd
also be an opportunity to fold redundant `tranpose(transpose(x))`
instances, avoiding the multi-output fusion altogether. For better
stability, this extension of the codegen is preferred as the first
step.

Signed-off-by: Artem Gindinson <gindinson@roofline.ai>
Assisted by: Codex

[Codegen] Support multi-output consumers with permuted indexing maps

Extend lowering of fused & tiled consumer ops from the basic case
(strictly identical indexing over the output operands). We now generalize
the logic for input indexing to support different output maps that are
simple permutations.

This allows to support some fusion cases where a simple transposition
from one of the consumer's connections get fused into the elementwise
generic, and then the consumer gets fused & tiled together with the
matmul. Whether we want such consumer fusion is a separate matter
subject to performance investigations, and in my reproducer there'd
also be an opportunity to fold redundant `tranpose(transpose(x))`
instances, avoiding the multi-output fusion altogether. For better
stability, this extension of the codegen is preferred as the first
step.

commit_message:
[Runtime][RISCV] Detect Zvfbfwma via hwprobe for the bf16 mmt4d ukernel

Without this bit being set the bf16 mmt4d tile functions added in #24695
are unreachable on every board: iree_uk_mmt4d_p() falls through to
iree_uk_mmt4d_select_tile_func_generic() and runs a generic scalar tile.

Define RISCV_HWPROBE_EXT_ZVFBFWMA (bit 54, per the kernel uapi
asm/hwprobe.h) and copy it alongside the neighbouring ZVFH/ZVFHMIN bits.
ZVFBFWMA is currently the only bf16 extension with a cpu_data feature
bit, so nothing else is added here.

Verified with iree-cpuinfo built for riscv64 on SpacemiT K3 board.
